newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh launches war on crop-eating rats.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh launches war on crop-eating rats.

text.p: Bangladesh has begun a massive hunt for rats that annually eat and destroy enough grain to feed three million people, government officials said on Monday.

They said Agriculture and Food Minister Begum Matia Chowdhury formally launched the month-long drive on Sunday, during which farmers will be taught rat-killing techniques. Successful rat killers will be rewarded with cash and crops.
Agriculture officials say up to 450,000 tonnes of paddy in the field are lost to rats each year, enough to feed up to three million people.
The rodents also destroy substantial quantity of grains in the warehouses, they said without giving details.
Bangladesh is almost self-sufficient in foodgrains with annual production of around 20 million tonnes, according to official figures. The country's population is about 118 million.
Rat killing has become an annual event in predominantly agricultural Bangladesh in recent years. Some 2.54 million rats were killed last year, agriculture officials said.
